About these figures

  • All figures are from the borough's adopted budgets: what Borough Council planned for each year, not what was actually spent or collected. Each year's figure comes from that year's budget (2016's from the 2017 budget).
  • They cover the budgets' summary of all operating funds: the General Fund, the Sewer & Solid Waste Fund, and the Liquid Fuels (highway) Fund.
  • Figures are shown as budgeted (nominal dollars). Choose “In 2026 dollars” to adjust them for inflation with the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI-U, U.S. city average, from the Bureau of Labor Statistics): each year's figure is multiplied by 2026's average price level divided by that year's. 2026's price level is the average of January to October 2026, the months published so far. October 2025 was not published (Data unavailable due to the 2025 lapse in appropriations), so 2025's average uses the other months.
  • Spending groups are the budgets' own: public safety (police and fire), public works (streets, sewer, trash & recycling, parks, vehicles), general government (administration, buildings, debt, grants, reserves) and community services (library, recreation, Town Center, seniors, PAC Center). Revenue sources group the budgets' revenue lines: other taxes are the real estate transfer and local services taxes; state aid is intergovernmental revenue; miscellaneous revenue includes police service contracts, permits, fines, contributions from Swarthmore College, interest and grants; prior-year funds are fund balances carried over from earlier years.
  • For every line's figures, sources and notes, see Explore a budget line.

Data, code, and the full method: https://github.com/diego519/Swarthmore-budget. This is an independent project, not affiliated with Swarthmore Borough; the borough's documents are the authoritative source.
